chapter_title_en: Wind Rising Overseas: The Eerie Black Armor
chapter_seo_title: Han Li Outsmarts a Spatial Restriction in the Void Heaven Palace – Chapter 477
chapter_meta_description: Han Li uses his Gold Devourer Beetles to create a temporary black armor that severs his connection to the spatial restriction, allowing him to steal two ancient treasures at once.
og_title: The Beetle-Armor That Fooled an Ancient Restriction – A Record of a Mortal's Journey to Immortality
og_description: In the Void Heaven Palace tower, Han Li performs a stunning heist: a living armor of tens of thousands of Gold Devourer Beetles lets him snatch not one, but two ancient treasures.
twitter_description: Han Li uses Gold Devourer Beetles to form a black energy-absorbing armor, stealing two treasures from an ancient restriction. #Xianxia #SmartProtagonist

lore_anchors.definition: A rare spirit insect that devours all forms of energy and metal; Han Li’s trump card for consuming magical attacks and bypassing restrictive barriers.
A high-grade formation that forcibly teleports anyone who triggers it out of a designated space; nearly impossible to counter without extreme power or master-level formation knowledge.
A magic weapon from a bygone era, distinct from modern tools; often possesses unique properties or unmatched power but cannot be absorbed into the body.
An ancient cloak-type treasure that flickers with blood-like light, likely granting defensive or aura-concealing abilities.
A set of five copper rings radiating five-colored light; a mysterious ancient treasure with a set-piece and considerable hidden potential.
A golden ancient treasure believed by Han Li to offer significant, straightforward power enhancement.
A collection of formation-breaking insights written by Xin Ruyin, a genius formation master; contains a theoretical conjecture on countering spatial restrictions that Han Li references.
The Gold Devourer Beetles’ ability to consume spiritual energy, allowing them to neutralize attacks and barriers that rely on continuous energy flow.
A formation that transfers a person from one location to another; in this chapter, it is the only artifact in the empty stone chamber where Han Li lands.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why did Han Li choose the cloak and the copper rings instead of the golden mirror?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The cloak offered immediate tactical utility for survival in the inner hall, while the copper rings were a high-risk, high-reward gamble on a set-piece surprise. The mirror was safe but predictable—not enough to justify using his beetle trick.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How did Han Li bypass the "only one treasure" rule?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He used the Gold Devourer Beetles to form a spiritual-absorption armor that temporarily severed his connection to the ambient energy, preventing the spatial restriction from detecting his contact with the first treasure and buying him time to grab a second.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the beetle-armor trick a one-time move or can Han Li repeat it?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The chapter frames it as a specific, high-execution gamble that worked with his existing beetle synergy. He could theoretically repeat it, but the armor is fragile under sustained pressure (as seen when it shattered), so it’s not a reliable daily strategy.
